pairs: Statera dolosa abominatio est apud Dominum,
A deceitful scale is an abomination with the Lord,
et pondus æquum voluntas ejus.
and a fair weighing is his will.
Ubi fuerit superbia,
Wherever arrogance may be,
ibi erit et contumelia;
there too is insult.
ubi autem est humilitas,
But wherever humility is,
ibi et sapientia.
there too is wisdom.
Simplicitas justorum diriget eos,
The simplicity of the just shall direct them,
et supplantatio perversorum vastabit illos.
and the rebellion of the perverse will devastate them.
Non proderunt divitiæ in die ultionis;
Wealth will not profit in the day of vengeance.
justitia autem liberabit a morte.
But justice shall liberate from death.
Justitia simplicis diriget viam ejus,
The justice of the simple shall direct his way.
et in impietate sua corruet impius.
And the impious will fall in his impiety.
Justitia rectorum liberabit eos,
The justice of the upright shall free them.
et in insidiis suis capientur iniqui.
And the iniquitous will be seized by their own treachery.
Mortuo homine impio,
When the impious man is dead,
nulla erit ultra spes,
there will no longer be any hope.
et exspectatio sollicitorum peribit.
And the expectation of the anxious will perish.
Justus de angustia liberatus est,
The just one is freed from anguish.
et tradetur impius pro eo.
And the impious one will be handed over instead of him.
Simulator ore decipit amicum suum;
The pretender deceives his friend by mouth.
justi autem liberabuntur scientia.
But the just shall be freed by knowledge.
In bonis justorum exsultabit civitas,
In the good of the just, the city shall exult.
et in perditione impiorum erit laudatio.
And in the perdition of the impious, there shall be praise.
Benedictione justorum exaltabitur civitas,
By the blessing of the just, the city shall be exalted.
et ore impiorum subvertetur.
And by the mouth of the impious, it will be subverted.
Qui despicit amicum suum indigens corde est;
Whoever despises his friend is destitute in heart.
vir autem prudens tacebit.
But the prudent man will remain silent.
Qui ambulat fraudulenter, revelat arcana;
Whoever walks dishonestly reveals secrets.
qui autem fidelis est animi, celat amici commissum.
But whoever is of a faithful soul conceals what is confided by a friend.
Ubi non est gubernator,
Where there is no governor,
populus corruet;
the people shall fall.
salus autem,
But where there is much counsel,
ubi multa consilia.
well-being shall be.
Affligetur malo qui fidem facit pro extraneo;
He will be afflicted with evil, who provides a guarantee for an outsider.
qui autem cavet laqueos securus erit.
But whoever is wary of traps shall be secure.
Mulier gratiosa inveniet gloriam,
A gracious woman shall discover glory.
et robusti habebunt divitias.
And the robust will have wealth.
Benefacit animæ suæ vir misericors;
A merciful man benefits his own soul.
qui autem crudelis est, etiam propinquos abjicit.
But whoever is cruel casts out even his close relatives.
Impius facit opus instabile,
The impious does work with inconstancy.
seminanti autem justitiam merces fidelis.
But for the sower of justice, there is the reward of faithfulness.
Clementia præparat vitam,
Clemency prepares life.
et sectatio malorum mortem.
And the pursuit of evils prepares death.
Abominabile Domino cor pravum,
A depraved heart is abominable to the Lord.
et voluntas ejus in iis qui simpliciter ambulant.
And his will is with those who walk in simplicity.
Manus in manu non erit innocens malus;
Hand in hand, the evil shall not be innocent.
semen autem justorum salvabitur.
But the offspring of the just shall be saved.
Circulus aureus in naribus suis,
A beautiful
mulier pulchra et fatua.
and senseless woman is like a gold ring in the snout of a swine.
Desiderium justorum omne bonum est;
The desire of the just is entirely good.
præstolatio impiorum furor.
The anticipation of the impious is fury.
Alii dividunt propria,
Some distribute their own goods,
et ditiores fiunt;
and they become wealthier.
alii rapiunt non sua,
Others seize what is not their own,
et semper in egestate sunt.
and they are always in need.
Anima quæ benedicit impinguabitur,
The soul that blesses shall be made fat.
et qui inebriat, ipse quoque inebriabitur.
And whoever inebriates will likewise be inebriated himself.
Qui abscondit frumenta maledicetur in populis;
Whoever hides away grain shall be cursed among the people.
benedictio autem super caput vendentium.
But a blessing is upon the head of those who sell it.
Bene consurgit diluculo qui quærit bona;
He does well to rise early,
qui autem investigator malorum est,
who seeks what is good.
opprimetur ab eis.
But whoever is a seeker of evils shall be oppressed by them.
Qui confidit in divitiis suis corruet:
Whoever trusts in his riches will fall.
justi autem quasi virens folium germinabunt.
But the just shall spring up like a green leaf.
Qui conturbat domum suam possidebit ventos,
Whoever troubles his own house will possess the winds.
et qui stultus est serviet sapienti.
And whoever is foolish will serve the wise.
Fructus justi lignum vitæ,
The fruit of the just one is the tree of life.
et qui suscipit animas sapiens est.
And whoever receives souls is wise.
Si justus in terra recipit,
If the just are repaid upon the earth,
quanto magis impius et peccator!
how much more the impious and the sinner!
